analysis:
Both units are base_text excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 887+ and 1326+). They are documentation only, with no code, config, or protocol changes in the visible text. No patch hunks were supplied, so I could not tell which lines changed. I found no executable security regression and no new attack surface.

The prose describes behaviors relevant to T-041 (SSD prefix cache) and TB-007. These are default-on encrypted SSD checkpoints, a 100 GiB ceiling limited to half of available disk, and a low-disk write guard. They also cover coordinator-authored cache scope, operator allowlists for network prefix caching, and the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=1 gate.

The changelog text says the shared SSD cache ceiling is raised to 100 GiB. The canonical T-041 says default is available-disk/2 with no fixed ceiling and a 20 GiB fallback. This is a documentation mismatch, not a code change, and the changelog is not authoritative for the threat model.

Later changelog sections mention a 'Tiers 2 and 3' note on 'Cache repeated user and model lookups'. The excerpt does not show auth or key-cache invalidation details, so I cannot assess revocation or staleness effects (T-004, T-053). The next pass should check the actual code for those changes.

Coverage limit: no source code was supplied, so claims in the changelog are unverified. The threat model T-041 may want a refresh if the 100 GiB ceiling and the cross-machine content-indexed holder lookup ship. Neither was evidenced beyond prose.
